description: Behavior-changing traps to avoid during the refactor pass. Every rule here protects a numeric or structural result that the automated re-QC would otherwise reject.

preserve_results.title: Never change a numeric or logical result while reshaping.
rule: The refactor is re-validated by QC against the reference datasets; any deviation is rejected and the original code is kept.
Reorganize freely (order of unrelated blocks, helper extraction, naming) but keep every computed value identical.
Do not 'simplify' a formula, rounding, or fillna default -- reproduce it exactly.
pitfalls: Swapping the order of two steps that share a dataset can change the result -- only reorder truly independent blocks.

preserve_index_and_dtype.title: Keep index handling and dtypes intact.
rule: Preserve `.reset_index(drop=True)` calls -- dropping them changes row labels and can change QC key alignment.
Do not introduce or remove `.copy()` in a way that turns a value assignment into a SettingWithCopy no-op.
Keep any explicit `.astype(...)` -- refactoring must not silently change a column's dtype.
pitfalls: Chaining operations that were previously separated by a `.copy()` can trigger a SettingWithCopyWarning and skip the write.

helper_side_effects.title: Beware in-place mutation when extracting helpers.
rule: A helper that mutates its DataFrame argument affects every later use of that frame; copy inside the helper or return a new frame.
Prefer returning the transformed frame and reassigning at the call site.
pitfalls: `df.drop(cols, inplace=True)` inside a helper mutates the caller's frame -- use `return df.drop(cols)` instead.
